title: Morphisms in a right localization are a colimit of ordinary Hom sets
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, let $S$ be a right multiplicative system of arrows, and let $Q':\mathcal C\to S^{-1}\mathcal C$ be its right localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For objects $M,N$ of $\mathcal C$, let $S/M$ be the category of arrows $t:P\to M$ in $S$, with morphisms the commuting triangles, and index by $(S/M)^{\mathrm{opp}}$. Then the canonical map $\varinjlim_{(t:P\to M)\in(S/M)^{\mathrm{opp}}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{S^{-1}\mathcal C}(Q'(M),Q'(N))$, sending $f:P\to N$ to $Q'(f)\circ Q'(t)^{-1}$, is a bijection.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0FND, label lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, proof line 9515, second equality; Categories Tag 05Q4, label categories-remark-right-localization-morphisms-colimit

proof.text: The displayed colimit is the colimit of sets of the functor $(S/M)^{\mathrm{opp}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$, $(t:P\to M)\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,N)$, with transition maps given by precomposition along morphisms of $S/M$; every element of it is the class of some $f:P\to N$ at some index $t$, and two pairs related by an index morphism have the same class. (By Stacks Tag 05Q4 the index category $S/M$ is cofiltered, so this colimit is filtered; the argument below does not use this.) The assignment $f\mapsto Q'(f)\circ Q'(t)^{-1}$ is compatible with these transition maps because a commuting triangle $t=t'\circ a$ gives $Q'(f\circ a)\circ Q'(t)^{-1}=Q'(f)\circ Q'(t')^{-1}$, so it defines the canonical map.

source.place: Categories, Remark 05Q4, definition of S/X and cofilteredness

proof.text: The assignment is surjective: for any $g:Q'(M)\to Q'(N)$, the right-fraction representation lemma supplies $P$, $t:P\to M$ in $S$, and $f:P\to N$ with $g=Q'(f)\circ Q'(t)^{-1}$, so $g$ is the image of the colimit class of $f$.

For injectivity, suppose representatives $f_i:P_i\to N$ over denominators $t_i:P_i\to M$ have the same localized morphism. The common-refinement lemma gives $R$ and $a_i:R\to P_i$ such that $t_1\circ a_1=t_2\circ a_2$ is in $S$ and $f_1\circ a_1=f_2\circ a_2$. These equalities say exactly that the two representatives become equal at the object $R$ of the indexing category, hence define the same element of the colimit.

The surjectivity and injectivity just proved show that the canonical map is a bijection. For the terminal case $S$ consisting only of identities, $S/M$ has terminal object $\mathrm{id}_M$ and the map reduces to the identity bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,N)$.
